_why: systemctl --failed only reports units that FAILED. A unit that was stopped or disabled is not failed -- it is absent, and absence is invisible to every 'what is running' view. tradeai-cio-telegram.service sat disabled for five days and no check anywhere could see it, because a disabled unit drops out of the very lists a monitor would enumerate. The only way to detect a missing thing is to have written down that it should be there.
_captured: 2026-09-13, from the live enabled set on ms01-openclaw.
_how_to_change: Deliberately retiring a unit? Remove it here in the same change that disables it. A diff in this file is the audit trail for 'we meant to turn that off'.

units._why: Polls the CIO bot (8751620457). It was disabled on 2026-09-08 and nobody noticed for five days; every reply the operator sent to a CIO alert landed in a room with no listener. This unit is the reason this manifest exists.
The health agent itself. If it stops, every other health signal stops with it and the silence looks like good news.
Wake path for the CIO worker. Died on inotify exhaustion 2026-09-12 and stayed failed for 14 hours.
Renders the tmpfs env every service reads. If it stops, secrets go stale and consumers fail in ways that do not name the cause.
The decision lane. Silent failure here means no decisions, which is indistinguishable from no signals.
